notes: Final file has 92 units. Units aligned one to one except for three splits: coder A coded the licensing and Bookstore routes as two units where coder B coded one (kept A split), and coder A merged equitable access and training into one unit that coder B split (kept B split). Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly general vs during-work or over-time, resolved by asking when the actor performs the act (syllabus categories became course-start, data rules during-work, standing commitments general); (2) modality, informs vs must/should for responsibility and expectation sentences, resolved to the sentence verb ("is responsible for", "is charged with", "must adapt", "is expected"); (3) policy_type, e.g. P56 vs P61 for scope, P17/P65 for licensing, P80/P09 vs P66 for instructor instruction, P70 vs P68 for modules for violators, P24 vs P48 for faculty disclosure, P31 vs P52 for the plagiarism check, P92 vs P50 for the approved-product data rule; (4) actor for staff and shared-voice rationale sentences; (5) document stance of the UMS IT guidance (A permit, B delegates), resolved to permit because it states conditions on use rather than handing the decision to instructors. 14 single-coder units were all checked against the text and kept (B found 11 mainly in the IT page: definitions, rationale and extra data warnings; A found 3). unit_stance disagreements (e.g. encourage vs neutral for rationale, require vs permit for disclosure) were also settled and recorded in resolution_why but are not scored.
